drills.a: JSON-RPC 2.0 over a transport (stdio or Streamable HTTP).

drills.q: Which primitive is model-controlled, and which is user-controlled?
drills.a: Tools are model-controlled; prompts are user-controlled. Resources are application-controlled.

drills.q: Why was HTTP+SSE deprecated as a transport?
drills.a: It required sticky sessions to route follow-up requests to the instance holding the open SSE stream, which broke horizontal scaling and had no clean resume after a drop.

drills.q: A tool throws an exception inside your MCP server. What should the client receive, and what happens if you get it wrong?
drills.a: A tools/call result with isError:true and descriptive content. Getting it wrong (letting it surface as a JSON-RPC error) raises a client-side exception that kills the whole agent run instead of giving the model an observation to react to.

drills.q: Explain why an MCP server is described as a 'confused deputy' by construction.
drills.a: It holds its own elevated credentials to a downstream system and acts on instructions from a model that can be manipulated by injected content (prompt injection via tool/resource output), so it can be tricked into misusing its own authority on an attacker's behalf.

drills.q: What is token passthrough, why is it forbidden, and what's the fix?
drills.a: Forwarding the client's token straight to a downstream API. Forbidden (spec MUST NOT) because it breaks audit trails and leaks user tokens if the server is compromised. Fix: validate the token's audience, then use a separately held, scoped credential for the downstream call.

drills.q: What is the headline change in the 2026-07-28 MCP spec revision?
drills.a: The protocol becomes stateless: the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake and Mcp-Session-Id sessions are removed; every request carries version/capabilities in _meta.

drills.q: Roots, Sampling, and Logging were all deprecated in the same spec revision. What replaces each?
drills.a: Roots -> pass paths as tool arguments or server config. Sampling -> call your own LLM provider directly. Logging -> stderr on stdio or OpenTelemetry.

drills.q: A remote MCP server behind a round-robin load balancer starts failing intermittently as traffic scales out. Diagnose and fix.
drills.a: Pre-2026-07-28 stateful mode: Mcp-Session-Id pins a session to one instance, and round-robin breaks that. Fix today: sticky sessions or a shared session store; long-term: migrate to the stateless transport.

drills.q: When should you NOT use MCP?
drills.a: When it's one agent calling one in-process function with no other consumer -- the protocol adds schema validation, serialization, and a subprocess/network round trip for no portability benefit.

drills.q: In one sentence, distinguish MCP from A2A.
drills.a: MCP connects an agent to tools and context; A2A connects agents to each other as peers with a task lifecycle -- they compose rather than compete.
